extracted.intended_audience: Royal Road users, authors, and site moderators/owners
extracted.subtask_description: A user forum post arguing the Royal Road rating/review system is vulnerable to abuse and suggesting accountability, detection, and moderation changes to prevent rate-bombing and ghost accounts. The post asks moderators/owners to track, identify, and sanction malicious reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach reviewer names and stated reasons to reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When a review/rating is done, a name should be attached and the reasons should be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: 1) Find ghost accounts 2) Verify the legitimacy of the review. The author argues that a simple review system with names/reasons would make the site more accurate rather than 'a complete sleezefest.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews should not remain anonymous to moderators/owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may be anonymous to authors/readers but should not remain anonymous to the moderators/owners of this site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators/owners should be able to see the identities (or linked histories) behind reviews so they can investigate and act on abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderators must have a review/rating interaction history per account
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators should have account histories equipped to their review/rating interactions, viewable only by mods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This history would allow moderators to target specific individuals who repeatedly engage in abusive rating behavior and provide evidence for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to detect obvious malicious attacks (rate-bombing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site/system should be able to detect obviously malicious attacks such as coordinated rate-bombing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poster asks: 'Are you guys at all able to detect these obviously malicious attacks?' — implying the system needs automated/statistical detection of suspicious patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and ban accounts that commit malicious rating
rubrics_metrics.description: If malicious accounts can be identified, they should be banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poster asks why known malicious accounts are not banned and urges enforcement (sanctions) against accounts that 'sink to this level to sow discord.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent mass creation/use of ghost accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The system should block or limit the ability to create ghost accounts en masse because when allowed, people will create many and abuse ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countermeasures could include verification, rate limits on new accounts, or other anti-abuse controls to reduce multi-account voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect abusive patterns via repeated identical ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated identical low/high scores (e.g., '.5,.5,.5' or '2.5,2.5,2.5') are evidence of foul play rather than sporadic legitimate ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pattern analysis (e.g., repeated same-value clusters) as a signal of rate-bombing; the poster cites observed incidents: '2.5x3 ratings' and '.5x3 ratings.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the power of anonymous users over novel rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: The system should not allow anonymous people to wield disproportionate influence over novels' reputations or visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post opens: 'why give anonymous people so much power over novels?' suggesting design changes (weighting, verification, or accountability) to reduce anonymous influence.
